spec.title: Service health
spec.description: One row per service. Each cell is a sparkline over the dashboard time range; the number beside it is the reduction shown in the column header tooltip: Status = last value (healthy host count), CPU / Response time / Requests = mean, 5xx = max. Click a service name to filter the whole dashboard to it.

spec.title: Memory
spec.description: Memory utilisation for each service, from the ECS metrics CloudWatch publishes. Metric names follow aws_<namespace>_<metric>_<statistic> with the CloudWatch name in snake case, so MemoryUtilization becomes memory_utilization.

spec.title: Error rate
spec.description: 5xx responses as a share of everything the service served. CloudWatch publishes a 5xx count only in minutes when a service returned one, so the numerator is absent for a healthy service; the trailing `or ... * 0` holds the line at zero where there is traffic, and leaves it absent where there is none. Threshold lines at 1% and 5%. The axis carries a soft max of 5%, so an idle panel sits at 0-5% with the threshold lines visible instead of Grafana inventing a 0-10000% range for an all-zero series; a real error rate above 5% expands it.

spec.expr:
sum(
  sum_over_time(aws_applicationelb_httpcode_target_5_xx_count_sum{dimension_LoadBalancer=~"app/fc-$stage.*", dimension_AvailabilityZone="", dimension_TargetGroup=~"targetgroup/fc-$stage-$service/.*"}[$__interval])
)
/
sum(
  sum_over_time(aws_applicationelb_request_count_sum{dimension_LoadBalancer=~"app/fc-$stage.*", dimension_AvailabilityZone="", dimension_TargetGroup=~"targetgroup/fc-$stage-$service/.*"}[$__interval])
)
or
sum(
  sum_over_time(aws_applicationelb_request_count_sum{dimension_LoadBalancer=~"app/fc-$stage.*", dimension_AvailabilityZone="", dimension_TargetGroup=~"targetgroup/fc-$stage-$service/.*"}[$__interval])
) * 0
